result.topic_en: Euler makes x^3 + n y^3 a square by factoring it with cube roots of unity and setting x + y∛n equal to the square of p + q∛n + r∛(nn). He gives parametric solutions and examples with sums of two cubes equal to a square. He then begins a more direct method using x+y=p, x−y=q.
result.transcription:
Quod uti est facillimum, ita casus, quo $x$ et $y$ sint inter se primi, maxime est difficilis. Formulae istius factor simplex est $x+y\sqrt[3]{n}$, et si $\alpha$ denotet unam radicem cubicam unitatis, ita ut sit $\alpha^3=1$, quam constat $\frac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}$, tum tertia radix cubica erit $\alpha\alpha$. Hinc formulae nostrae $x^3+ny^3$ alius factor simplex erit $x+\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n}$, ac tertius $x+\alpha\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n}$; ita ut formula nostra futura sit productum horum trium factorum
$(x+y\sqrt[3]{n})(x+\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n})(x+\alpha\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n})$,
qui singuli factores reddantur quadrata, hoc modo, quo statim patet, si unus fuerit quadratus, etiam reliquos fore quadratos.
Posito enim $x+y\sqrt[3]{n}=(p+q\sqrt[3]{n}+r\sqrt[3]{nn})^2$, per naturam rei fiet
$x+\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n}=(p+\alpha q\sqrt[3]{n}+\alpha\alpha r\sqrt[3]{nn})^2$ et $x+\alpha\alpha y\sqrt[3]{n}=(p+\alpha\alpha q\sqrt[3]{n}+\alpha r\sqrt[3]{nn})^2$.
Productum ergo, quod est $x^3+ny^3$, etiam erit quadratum, et quidem rationale, quippe cujus radix erit
$p^3+nq^3+nnr^3-3npqr$.
Tantum igitur opus est, primam illam positionem supra datam evolvi, ex qua consequimur
$x+y\sqrt[3]{n}=pp+2pq\sqrt[3]{n}+2pr\sqrt[3]{nn}$
$+2nqr+nrr\sqrt[3]{n}+qq\sqrt[3]{nn}$,
unde statim sequitur fore $x=pp+2nqr$, $y=2pq+nrr$.
Praeterea vero esse oportet $2pr+qq=0$, unde $r=-\frac{qq}{2p}$. Sumatur ergo $p=2aa$ et $r=-bb$, fietque $q=2ab$, consequenter valores satisfacientes sunt
$x=4a(a^3-nb^3)$ et $y=b(8a^3-nb^3)$.
Aliter. Si ponatur $p=aa$ et $r=-2bb$, erit $q=2ab$ et $x=a(a^3-8nb^3)$ et $y=4b(a^3+nb^3)$, ubi $a$ et $b$ pro lubitu assumere licet.
Exemplum. Quaerantur duo cubi inter se primi $x^3$ et $y^3$, quorum summa fiat quadratum, cujusmodi quidem statim sunt obvii 1 et 8. Hic ob $n=1$, erit
$x=a(a^3-8b^3)$ et $y=4b(a^3+b^3)$.
Sit $a=3$, $b=1$, erit $x=57$, $y=112$, quorum cuborum summa fit quadratum, cujus radix $=1261$.
Sit $a=2$, $b=-1$, erit $x=32$, $y=-28$, sive $x=8$, $y=-7$.
In hac tamen solutione, etsi generalis videtur, casus quo $x=1$ et $y=2$ non continetur, cujus ratio sine dubio in eo est quaerenda, quod hoc casu numerus $n$ ipse sit cubus, ideoque irrationalitas evanescat. Quod clarius patebit ex solutione magis directa, nam ut $x^3+y^3$ fiat quadratum, ponatur $x+y=p$ et $x-y=q$, ut sit $x=\frac{p+q}{2}$ et $y=\frac{p-q}{2}$, unde fit
$x^3+y^3=\frac{p^3+3pqq}{4}=\frac{(pp+3qq)p}{4}$,
quae formula ut reddatur quadrata, debet esse $p(pp+3qq)$ quadratum, unde si hi duo factores sint inter se primi, uterque factor quadratum esse debet. Posterius vero tantum locum habet, si $p$ divisibile sit per 3. Hinc duos casus evolvi convenit.
I. Sint hi factores inter se primi, atque ut $pp+3qq$ fiat quadratum, vidimus sumi debere $p=ff-3gg$ et $q=2fg$; at vero ut et $p$ fiat quadratum, capiatur $f=hh+3kk$ et $g=2hk$. Ergo solutio hinc nata erit
$x=\frac{h^4+4h^3k-6hhkk+12hk^3+9k^4}{2}$, $y=\frac{h^4-4h^3k-6hhkk-12hk^3+9k^4}{2}$.

methods.what: Factorisation of x^3+ny^3 into three linear factors using a cube root of unity α
Setting the first factor equal to a square in Q(∛n) makes the conjugate factors squares as well, so the product is a rational square
Square root of x^3+ny^3 given by the norm form
Comparing coefficients gives x, y and the condition 2pr+qq=0
Numerical example: two cubes whose sum is a square
methods.quote: Sit $a=3$, $b=1$, erit $x=57$, $y=112$, quorum cuborum summa fit quadratum, cujus radix $=1261$.

methods.what: Direct method via x+y=p, x−y=q, reducing to p(pp+3qq) being a square
Resulting quartic parametric solution in the case where the factors are coprime

items.quote: ita casus, quo $x$ et $y$ sint inter se primi, maxime est difficilis
items.english: the case in which x and y are coprime is the most difficult

items.quote: si unus fuerit quadratus, etiam reliquos fore quadratos
items.english: if one is a square, the others will also be squares

items.quote: Quaerantur duo cubi inter se primi $x^3$ et $y^3$, quorum summa fiat quadratum
items.english: Let two mutually prime cubes x^3 and y^3 be sought whose sum is a square

items.quote: casus quo $x=1$ et $y=2$ non continetur, cujus ratio sine dubio in eo est quaerenda, quod hoc casu numerus $n$ ipse sit cubus, ideoque irrationalitas evanescat
items.english: the case x=1, y=2 is not contained in this solution; the reason is doubtless to be sought in the fact that here n is itself a cube, so the irrationality vanishes

items.quote: Posterius vero tantum locum habet, si $p$ divisibile sit per 3.
items.english: The latter [the factors not being coprime] occurs only if p is divisible by 3.
Hence it is fitting to work out two cases.
